itineraries.title: Wat and Peace - 2 Day Itinerary
editorial: We spent two nights in Siem Reap, which is the gateway to Angkor Wat and other temples in the area. Siem Reap has an international airport with direct flights from major Southeast Asian cities. If flight timings permit, we suggest reaching Siem Reap a day prior to the temple tour and indulging in activities around the town.
What if we had more time?

If we had a little more time, we’d drop by the capital, Phnom Penh. Mostly to get experience a more authentic Cambodian way of life, which isn’t always evident in the manicured Siem Reap. And of course, to learn more about the horrors of the genocide.

days.title: Day 1 - Siem Reap
editorial: Cambodia is home to the grace and intricate Apsara dance. There are various venues across Siem Reap that host performances in the evening alongside a lavish buffet. We visited Amazon Angkor, a rather fancy banquet that we reached by wading through some not-so-fancy (but entirely safe) back alleys.

The Apsara show goes on from 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM, after which you can take your lot to Pub Street, a quintessential Southeast Asian party street. But remember, the sunrise temple tour starts at 5:00 AM, so tuck yourself in by a reasonable time.

days.title: Day 2 - Angkor Wat
editorial: Day two is devoted to temples. Be sure to book your tour in advance especially if you’re visiting in the peak season. We booked ours with {tour operator} via Klook and had a great time with Chanthy. Our tour covered the temples of Angkor Wat, Bayon, Ta Prohm, and Banteay Kdei.

Seeing the sun rise over Angkor Wat is a sight for the Gods (duh!). Those 30 minutes alone make the trip to Cambodia worth it. You spend the morning exploring all the temples before it starts getting hot.

In the afternoon, when the sun is blazing overhead, you can head back to Angkor Wat (on your own) and pretty much have the view to yourself. My wife and I got some great pictures in our return to the temple.
